answer: Each agent must lock a staked bond behind every verified claim, and independent peers who re-execute the work can challenge it; a contradiction triggers slashing, so a sybil farm must fund a real bond per fake identity and risks losing all of it on a single detected lie. Honest actors treat the bond as a refundable pearl of reputation, while the attacker's cost climbs linearly with each puppet. The knoll of trust is thus built from capital at risk, not names, and one caught falsehood sends a ripple through every identity tied to that stake.
